Question: Let \(\mathbb R_+\) denote the positive real numbers. Let \(\mathcal M\subseteq \mathbb R^n\) be a nondegenerate submanifold, and let \(\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n:\mathbb R_+\to(0,1)\) be non-increasing functions. A point \(x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)\in\mathbb R^n\) is called \((\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n)\)-approximable if there exist infinitely many integers \(q\ge 1\) and integers \(p_1,\dots,p_n\) such that \(|qx_i-p_i|<\psi_i(q)\) for every \(i\). Which statement gives the correct criterion, in terms of \(\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi_1(q)\cdots \psi_n(q)\), for whether almost all points of \(\mathcal M\) (with respect to the induced Lebesgue measure on \(\mathcal M\)) are \((\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n)\)-approximable?
Predicted label: 'E'
Predicted text: 'A sufficient condition is that \\(\\sum_{q=1}^\\infty \\psi_1(q)\\cdots\\psi_n(q)\\) diverges: in that case the set of \\((\\psi_1,\\dots,\\psi_n)\\)-approximable points on \\(\\mathcal M\\) has full measure, without asserting the converse or the convergent case.'
Correct label: 'D'
Correct text: 'The set of \\((\\psi_1,\\dots,\\psi_n)\\)-approximable points on \\(\\mathcal M\\) has full measure (with respect to the induced Lebesgue measure on \\(\\mathcal M\\)) if \\(\\sum_{q=1}^\\infty \\psi_1(q)\\cdots \\psi_n(q)\\) diverges, and has measure zero if that series converges.'
Exact Match: 0.0
